Lucid’s Cosmos Sub-$50K EV Imagined, Do You Like the Design?
6 photos
Photo: Kolesa
Lucid Motors has three main models in its current lineup . These are called the Air, Gravity, and Sapphire, and EV enthusiasts (and not only) know everything there is to know about them.
Is there room for improvement in the company’s current portfolio? The answer to this question is obviously yes, and the automaker is doing just that. You likely know that Lucid has a more affordable electric vehicle in the making, because it was supposed to hit the assembly line at the end of the year (2026). However, it was eventually delayed, and now interested parties will have to wait until the second half of 2027 to get their hands on it.
The model is called the Lucid Cosmos , and it will be the auto marque’s first vehicle fully built at their plant. In case you forgot, it is a crossover that will take on the likes of the Tesla Model Y and Rivian R2, and will be priced at under $50,000. The entry-level grade is expected to kick off in the high $40,000s, though opting for a better-equipped model, supposedly with more oomph available on tap, might require paying over $70,000.
Lucid’s Cosmos is understood to be based on a new platform, which will also be the foundation stone of the Earth, because the Cosmos is not the only model in the pipeline. Further more, a third vehicle, whose name is yet unknown, will be based on this construction as well. New motors are understood to be on deck, though details surrounding the output and thrust are unknown at this point, and will be released in due course.
Photo: Kolesa Now, while we may not know much about the Lucid Cosmos , we do know what it will look like. That’s because a set of patent images surfaced a few months ago, revealing the styling of the upcoming model from a few angles. And guess what? These drawings served as a foundation stone for the digital illustrations signed by Nikita Chuyko, which were shared online by Kolesa recently.
The model features a tiny grille between the slim LED headlights. The Lucid name is visible above, and further down, we can see a quite large air intake in the middle of the bumper, flanked by the vertical vents. The front fascia looks similar to the one of the larger Gravity, for what it’s worth, and to be honest, we wouldn’t be surprised if this thing featured a light bar at the front, though it is not present in the renderings shared in the gallery.
Further up, we can see a rather small front hood with angular curves on it. The profile looks quite soft for the most part, and this applies to the design of the doors and the roofline. The Lucid Cosmos features flush door handles, and has some angular styling on the lower parts of the doors. Further back, the model features a split-style rear windscreen, a floating-like design for the rear pillars, and a sporty wing stretching across the rear windscreen.
The tailgate is decorated with the backlit Lucid logo, which sits between the ultra thin taillights. The rear bumper also features a quite angular design. We can also see the horizontal reflectors on the lower outer edges, as well as a diffuser-like element. The license plate recess is visible on the bumper. There is way of knowing whether the Lucid lettering will be backlit, or if there will be a light bar stretching across the width of the tailgate as hinted in the patent drawings.
Photo: Kolesa Do you know how most patent images focus solely on the exterior of an upcoming car ? Well, these ones also offered an important glimpse inside. The dashboard panel seems to be dominated by a large screen, and it is yet unknown whether this thing will be split in half, or if there will be three displays, including perhaps one for the front passenger.
The center console has a pair of dials on it, as well as storage further back, and we can also see a pair of air vents for the backseat occupants, and a small cubby above them. Chances are that higher grades will feature rear-seat HVAC controls, too.
Overall, we can say that the upcoming Lucid Cosmos will borrow a few things from the larger Gravity, but it will also carve its own path at the same time, and only time will tell if it is a winning recipe or not. God knows that Lucid deserves a break, because it is struggling. The company is said to have delivered less than 4,000 vehicles in the second quarter of the year, so it likely hopes that the Cosmos might boost their sales overall.
If you were into mid-sized EVs and you saw the Lucid Cosmos looking like it does in these otherwise realistic (for the most part) renderings , would you spend your money on it?
